method: Three parallel independent model completions; not autonomous repository agents

responses.text:
**Strongest objection:** The patch hardens surfaces while the core claim stays unvalidated. Strict gates failing on Redis, issuer pin, and supply/demand health means you're polishing a system whose *measurement validity* is untested—no independent calibration, no retention data, no paid pilots. Injected timeout recovery failing while immediate dispatch works suggests your failure model is wrong, not just buggy: recovery logic diverges from production reality. Launching a "responsible beta" with degraded sources displayed and no proven 100x outcome is marketing a hypothesis as infrastructure. The mirror-provenance work is good engineering in service of an unproven premise.

**Unconventional alternative:** Invert the roadmap—make evidence the product. Ship a free, read-only "audit mode": users submit their own traffic, receive raw capsule data, and independently verify the crowding heuristic against their own outcomes. This converts your missing calibration into distributed, adversarial validation *before* billing exists. Kill agents entirely; they compound unvalidated claims.

**Go/no-go:**

**No-go if:** timeout recovery fails re-test; any strict gate fails in production topology; a third party cannot reproduce crowding scores from raw capsules; no independent calibration exists by September 1, 2026.

**Go if:** all 13 checks pass in production-mirrored config; independent calibration reproduces scores within stated tolerance; degraded-source mode survives a chaos drill; you publish the beta's confidence interval and what "no proven outcome" means to users, verbatim.

Default posture: no-go. Earn the launch.

**Strongest objection:** Your gates test infrastructure, not truthfulness. Four models answering 12/13 checks proves orchestration works—not that the crowding heuristic or evidence capsules produce calibrated, non-hallucinated output. A failing injected-timeout check is noise; unvalidated claim provenance across seven supply adapters is the actual launch risk. You're hardening the pipe while the water is untested.

**Unconventional alternative:** Skip billing and agents entirely. Ship as a read-only "reproducibility instrument": every capsule carries its full supply-chain provenance, seeded prompts, and a public re-run harness so external researchers can independently verify outputs. Your differentiation isn't features—it's being the only research beta whose evidence is independently checkable. That converts "no customer evidence" from a weakness into the thesis, and it's the cheapest possible hardening with the highest trust yield.

**Go/no-go (Sep–Oct 2026):**
- **GO if:** all five strict gates green under chaos (including timeout recovery fixed); ≥100 independently re-run capsules match signed outputs; degraded-source UX passes adversarial review; provenance audit by one external party.
- **NO-GO if:** any gate requires manual intervention to pass; mirror rejection in strict canary produces false positives >2%; supply/demand health degrades without automatic user-visible notice; or you cannot demonstrate the timeout failure root cause—not just the fix.

**Challenge to your framing:** "Launch responsibly" with strict gates failing is an oxymoron. Fix the 13th check or delay. Billing now would monetize an uncalibrated product—stop debating it.

**Strongest objection:** The patch treats integrity as a display problem (provenance, notices, degraded-source labels) while strict gates still fail and timeout recovery is broken. Signed capsules saying "this data is degraded" are, functionally, a product whose core promise — reliable simultaneity — is unproven. You're engineering trust theater: integrity metadata on top of bars nobody has independently calibrated. Worse, the plan to "launch responsibly" has no load-bearing evidence — zero pilots, zero retention data, zero calibration. A cleaner mirror rejection won't fix that the gateway itself recovers unreliably.

**Unconventional high-leverage alternative:** Radical scope cut, not more adapters or agents. Kill six supply adapters and launch **one vertical, one adapter, strict-mode only** — a tiny product that passes *all*
